facts.statement: Buriolestes lived during the Late Triassic in the Paraná Basin of southern Brazil.
facts.quote: Buriolestes is a genus of early sauropodomorph dinosaurs from the Late Triassic Santa Maria Formation of the Paraná Basin in southern Brazil.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Buriolestes was discovered in 2009 in the Buriol ravine in Brazil.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, ULBRA-PVT280, was discovered in 2009 in the Buriol ravine in São João do Polêsine, Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus name Buriolestes was coined in 2016, combining the Buriol family name with the Greek word for "robber."
facts.quote: In 2016, the holotype specimen was described and given the generic name Buriolestes, after the Buriol family; the suffix -lestes is Greek for "robber."

facts.statement: The species name schultzi honors the paleontologist Cezar Schultz.
facts.quote: The specific name honors palaeontologist Cezar Schultz.

facts.statement: Buriolestes likely fed on small vertebrates and invertebrates based on the shape of its teeth.
facts.quote: The shape of the teeth of Buriolestes suggest that it was a carnivore which fed on small vertebrates and invertebrates

facts.statement: Mature Buriolestes specimens show significant size variation, ranging from 6.4 kg to over 15.4 kg.
facts.quote: Skeletally mature specimens of Buriolestes exhibit intraspecific variation through size disparity, with one robust individual weighing over 15.4 kg and others weighing between 6.4 - 7.2 kg.

facts.statement: A 2020 study indicated that Buriolestes had brain morphology similar to that of crocodiles.
facts.quote: A 2020 study by Rodrigo T. Müller et al. that analysed Buriolestes endocranial anatomy indicated a similar brain morphology to crocodiles.

facts.statement: Buriolestes was likely a sight-based predator because it had a well-developed optic lobe and a comparatively underdeveloped olfactory bulb.
facts.quote: The well-developed optic lobe suggests that Buriolestes was a sight-based predator, as its olfactory bulb was comparatively underdeveloped.

facts.statement: A 2022 study found that the bones of Buriolestes were not pneumatized and lacked an invasive air sac system.
facts.quote: In 2022, Aureliano and colleagues performed a mirco-computed tomography scan on the postcranial skeletons of some of the earliest saurischian dinosaurs that lived during the late Carnian including Gnathovorax with sauropodomorphs Pampadromaeus and Buriolestes, which showed that the invasive air sac system was absent and that their bones were not pneumatised.

facts.statement: Other analyses based on the original dataset place Buriolestes as the single most basal sauropodomorph.
facts.quote: The other three analyses, which also corresponded to the original description's dataset, agreed with that study's placement of Buriolestes as the single most basal sauropodomorph.

facts.statement: Buriolestes lived approximately between 237 and 228 million years ago in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el a finales del Triásico hace aproximadamente entre 237 a 228 millones de años en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ULBRA-PVT280 was discovered at the Buriol site in São João do Polêsine, Brazil.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, ULBRA-PVT280, fue descubierto en el sitio Buriol en São João do Polêsine, en Brasil.

facts.statement: The rocks containing the fossils belong to the Santa Maria Formation, which dates to the Carnian age.
facts.quote: Estas rocas forman parte de la formación Santa María, la cual data de la época del Carniense.

facts.statement: The specimen consists of a single skeleton preserving parts of the skull, vertebrae, and the left front and hind legs.
facts.quote: El espécimen consiste de un único esqueleto que preserva partes del cráneo, vértebras, la pata delantera y la pata trasera izquierdas.

facts.statement: The genus was named and described in 2016 by the Buriol family who owned the land, with the suffix -lestes derived from the Greek word for "thief".
facts.quote: El espécimen fue nombrado y descrito en 2016, con el nombre de Buriolestes por la familia Buriol, propietaria del terreno; el sufijo -lestes proviene del griego para "ladrón".

facts.statement: The species name honors the paleontologist Cezar Schultz.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra al paleontólogo Cezar Schultz.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis published in 2016 confirmed Buriolestes' affinities with sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado en 2016 confirmó las afinidades de Buriolestes con los sauropodomorfos.

facts.statement: Buriolestes belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: Buriolestes is classified within the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Buriolestes lived during the Carnian stage, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The shape of Buriolestes' teeth suggests it was a predator that fed on small invertebrates and vertebrates.
facts.quote: La forma de los dientes de Buriolestes sugiere que era un depredador que se alimentaba de invertebrados y vertebrados pequeños

facts.statement: This provides evidence for the idea that sauropodomorphs, and likely all saurischians and dinosaurs as a whole, were ancestrally carnivorous.
facts.quote: lo cual proporciona evidencia a la idea de que los sauropodomorfos y probablemente todos los saurisquios y los dinosaurios en su conjunto fueron ancestralmente carnívoros

facts.statement: The association of Buriolestes and Ixalerpeton recalls the simultaneous presence of dinosaurian and non-dinosaurian dinosauromorphs at other sites.
facts.quote: La asociación de Buriolestes e Ixalerpeton recuerda la presencia simultánea de dinosauromorfos dinosaurios y no dinosaurios en otros sitios

rejected.quote: Although Buriolestes superficially resembles predatory theropod dinosaurs, with jaws lined by finely serrated and slightly curved teeth well-adapted to a carnivorous diet, it is in fact an early member of the otherwise-herbivorous Sauropodomorpha
